decisions.reason: As a manual laser marking workstation that extends the firm’s established laser and integration capabilities, it remains well within the firm’s absorptive capacity and is more likely to be refined through in-house R&D and service feedback than withdrawn.

This thermal inkjet printer is very close to the firm’s core coding applications and customer base, so the firm can readily absorb user feedback and improve it through its existing development, production and support system.

Although piezo inkjet is somewhat more specialized and may require more learning, it still fits the firm’s knowledge base in industrial marking and is likely to be retained as the firm deepens capabilities across printing technologies.

As a flagship 2024 launch shown prominently on the home page and strongly aligned with the firm’s strategic move toward digitalized identification and traceability, these industrial laser systems are very unlikely to be taken off the market soon.

The compact laser marking cabin builds directly on the firm’s existing laser portfolio and operating concept, making it a product the firm can support and improve efficiently with its established technical and service resources.

Despite being application-specific, this lubricant printing system builds on the firm’s high-resolution marking know-how and its award recognition suggests valuable market validation that the firm can exploit rather than abandon.
